styleAbout.paragraph: Forest psytrance is a subgenre of psychedelic trance that emerged in the early 2000s, primarily from the Scandinavian underground scene. Rooted in the spirit of outdoor gatherings and night-time forest parties, it developed as a reaction to the more commercial and melodic directions that mainstream psytrance was taking at the time.

The sound of forest psytrance is defined by its dark, earthy and deeply organic character. Basslines are typically rolling, heavy and hypnotic, sitting low in the mix and driving the track forward with an almost ritualistic momentum. Percussion is intricate and layered, often featuring complex polyrhythmic patterns that reward attentive listening on the dancefloor.

Atmospherically, forest psytrance draws heavily from nature — animal recordings, processed organic sounds, insects, wind and water are frequently woven into the sound design. This creates a feeling of being deep in a forest at night, surrounded by unknown creatures and ancient energies. The music is intentionally immersive and often unsettling, designed to push the listener into altered states of consciousness.

Typical BPM range sits between 146 and 150, allowing the bassline to breathe and the atmospheres to develop fully. Tracks are usually long — often exceeding eight minutes — giving the music time to build, evolve and take the listener on a complete journey.

Key influences and pioneering artists in the global forest psytrance scene include Derango, Traskel, Drone Bixie, Jahbo,  Grapes Of Wrath and Ka-Sol. Labels such as Parvati Records, Yggdrasil Records, Sanaton Records, Schlabaduerst Records and Stoneage Records helped establish and define the genre internationally throughout the 2000s and 2010s.

Moon Koradji Records has been part of the forest psytrance community since its founding in 2007 in Kyiv, Ukraine. The label has always gravitated towards the darker, more organic end of the psychedelic spectrum, releasing music from artists across Scandinavia, Eastern Europe, Japan, North & South America and beyond who share a common vision of deep, forest-rooted sound design.

The Scandinavian influence on forest psytrance cannot be overstated. Swedish and Norwegian producers in particular developed a distinctive flavour of the genre — sometimes called 'Scando forest' — characterised by exceptionally clean production, playful yet dark sound design, and a unique sense of humour hidden within the twisted atmospheres. Many of Moon Koradji's most celebrated artists come from this tradition.

Today forest psytrance remains a thriving underground movement, celebrated at outdoor festivals and small forest gatherings around the world. Events such as Ozora Festival in Hungary, Boom Festival in Portugal, and countless smaller regional gatherings continue to provide a spiritual home for forest psytrance artists and their dedicated community of listeners.

styleAbout.paragraph: Dark psytrance (also known as darkpsy) is a subgenre of psychedelic trance that emerged as a recognizable style after 2003, primarily from the underground scenes in Germany and Russia. It evolved from late-1990s experimental works that pushed the heavier, darker boundaries of psytrance, serving as a reaction to the more melodic and commercial directions that mainstream psytrance was taking at the time.

The sound of dark psytrance is defined by its cold, intense and synthetic character. Basslines are heavy, rolling and often distorted, sitting prominently in the mix with aggressive drive and pitch-shifting energy. Synths are twisted, glitchy and full of alien textures, while percussion layers complex polyrhythms and rapid-fire kicks that create a relentless, hypnotic momentum.

Atmospherically, dark psytrance draws heavily from dark ambient, industrial and horror influences — featuring spooky special effects, laser-like sweeps, horror-film vocal samples, and cybernetic sound design. This creates a feeling of entering an alien dimension or confronting the unknown, with themes of death, night, transcendence and eschatological depth. The music is intentionally immersive and often unsettling, designed to propel the listener into profound altered states of consciousness.

Typical BPM range sits between 148 and 160, allowing the high-energy drive and complex sound design to breathe while maintaining a furious dancefloor intensity. Tracks are usually long — often exceeding eight minutes — giving the music space to build intricate layers, evolve through atmospheric sections and deliver complete sonic journeys.

Key influences and pioneering artists in the global dark psytrance scene include Xenomorph, X-Dream, Para Halu. Labels such as Bhooteshwara Records, Zenon Records, DejaVu Records and Discovalley Records helped define and spread the genre internationally throughout the 2000s and 2010s.

Moon Koradji Records has been part of the dark psytrance community since its founding in 2007. The label has always gravitated towards the darker, more intense and cyberdelic end of the psychedelic spectrum, releasing music from artists across Russia, Germany, Scandinavia, Eastern Europe, Brazil and beyond who share a common vision of raw, high-energy sound design.

The Russian and German influence on dark psytrance cannot be overstated. Russian producers in particular developed a distinctive flavour of the genre — sometimes referred to as the 'Russian style' or cyberdelic — characterised by exceptionally intricate production, cold synthetic textures, alien soundscapes and relentless drive. Many of Moon Koradji's darker releases draw directly from this powerful tradition.

Today dark psytrance remains a vital underground force, celebrated at night-time forest gatherings, high-energy festivals and dedicated dark stages around the world. Events such as Ozora Festival in Hungary, Boom Festival in Portugal, and countless regional parties continue to provide a spiritual home for dark psytrance artists and their fiercely dedicated global community.
